top.title: Who is Arjun Rajput? The left-handed batter who came to India's rescue against Pakistan in U19 Asia Cup
top.description: NEW DELHI: India’s Under-19 batter Arjun Rajput came to his team's rescue with a brilliant century against Pakistan in the U-19 Asia Cup on Sunday. The youngster from Jalandhar showed great composure when India were struggling at 22/3 after choosing to bat first at the Ministry Turf 1. Rajput walked in at No. 5, with the team desperately needing a partnership. However, Aaryavir Sehwag, son of former India opener Virender Sehwag, could score only 22 off 40 balls. Anvay Dravid, son of former India captain and coach Rahul Dravid, also failed to make a significant contribution. With wickets falling at the other end, Rajput took responsibility and played attacking cricket. He used sweeps against spinners and played aerial shots against fast bowlers to put pressure back on Pakistan. He scored 107 off 85 balls, hitting 11 fours and five sixes, before getting dismissed. His innings helped India reach 208 before being bowled out in 46.3 overs. Who is Arjun Rajput? The 18-year-old from Jalandhar, Punjab, received his first call-up to India's Under-19 team in July this year. He had an impressive run in the 2026-27 Under-19 Vinoo Mankad Trophy, where he scored 695 runs in eight innings and helped Punjab win the title. He also scored an unbeaten 55 off 33 balls in the final. Rajput had earlier made headlines playing for Ludhiana Lions in the Sher-E-Punjab T20 Cup, where he smashed 78 off just 46 balls against Mohali. Cricket runs in his passion, but his family background is a humble one. The youngster's journey to the India U-19 team has been shaped by years of hard work and family sacrifices. His father, Hoti Ram, initially earned a living by selling chhole-kulche from a roadside cart in Jalandhar. He later moved to a small bakery, from where he continues to prepare and deliver kulchas. Speaking about his son's journey, he told NDTV Sports, “I have been making kulchas for many years. Arjun has been playing cricket since the age of five years. He is very talented and hardworking.” Rajput began training at the Harbhajan Singh Cricket Academy before continuing his development under coach Vikram Sidhu. He also contributed with the ball against Nepal in India's tournament opener, taking three wickets for just eight runs.

top.title: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Ben Shelton in thrilling final for first Paris Masters title
top.description: Carlos Alcaraz ’s excellent comeback continued as he defeated Ben Shelton 7-6(5) 7-5 to claim the Paris Masters title for the first time. World No 3 Alcaraz missed nearly five months of the 2026 season with a wrist injury and his initial comeback came to an end at Shelton’s hands, with the American triumphing in a epic five-setter in the US Open quarter-finals. Since then Alcaraz has lifted ATP 500 titles in Tokyo and Vienna, the latter just last week. Despite not playing at his fluid best he scraped through in Paris - saving two match points against Taylor Fritz in the quarter-finals - and he continued his late-season surge with victory in an entertaining encounter between two of the tour’s flair players and his first meeting with Shelton since New York. Shelton made an assured start on serve and it was Alcaraz who came under pressure first, falling 0-40 down as the American led 2-1. But the Spaniard saved four break points to hold in a near eight-minute game, with a combination of deft volleys and aggression from the back of the court. Both players struggled to take their chances as Shelton saved two break points - one with a sublime angled volley - to keep things on serve for a 4-3 lead, then spurned another two chances to break before Alcaraz held for 4-4 with a punishing, unreturned first serve. Inevitably the first set went to a tiebreak, a contest of frequent momentum swings as eight of the 12 points went against serve. Shelton battled back from 1-3 down with an explosive smash while back-pedalling to the baseline, but could not press his advantage home. Alcaraz set up two set points with a fierce backhand volley, spurning the first thanks to an unhelpful net cord which just dipped back onto his side, but let out a roar of relief as Shelton blasted a forehand wide to concede the first set 7-6(5) in just over an hour. US Open runner-up Shelton won his previous three matches in Paris in three sets and would be forced to attempt another escape act, starting from 0-30 down in his first service game of the second set. A superb overhead smash from the American in the next game led to the first sign of genuine frustration for Alcaraz, who mimed throwing his racquet to the ground, as Shelton held to love. The seven-time major winner was not at his best but took advantage of a dip in concentration by Shelton to break back to 15 in his next service game, levelling things for 4-4. top.title: Garcia, Schick take Leverkusen to derby win at Cologne
top.description: Freiburg can climb to third spot with a win at home over strugglers Union Berlin on Sunday (Silas Stein) Goals from Aleix Garcia and Patrik Schick took Bayer Leverkusen to a tense 2-1 derby win at Cologne on Sunday, lifting the visitors to fifth in the Bundesliga table. Garcia curled an excellent effort into the top corner after just seven minutes and Schick scored five minutes from time in a fiery encounter which produced 11 yellow cards, including six for the hosts. Germany starlet Said El Mala scored a stoppage-time consolation goal for the hosts, who sit in 15th spot, just one clear of the relegation playoff placing. One of several derbies in Germany's football-mad north-west, Cologne and Leverkusen are just 10 kilometres (six miles) apart. The travelling support teased the hosts with chants referring to the 2023-24 season, when Leverkusen won their maiden Bundesliga title and Cologne were relegated. Leverkusen broke through just seven minutes in when Garcia's free-kick flew over the wall and into the top-left corner, with a helpless Cologne goalie Marvin Schwaebe watching on. Just before the break, the Spaniard found Jarell Quansah in space but the England centre-back headed just wide. Well handled by the Leverkusen defence, the hosts grew increasingly frustrated, picking up five of their six yellow cards in the second-half. Schick had a goal rubbed out for handball with ten minutes to go but broke through just five minutes later, slotting in on the counter for an eighth goal in nine league games this season. El Mala scored one of his own in stoppage time but the goal came too late to launch a Cologne comeback. Later on Sunday, Freiburg can climb to third spot with a win at home over strugglers Union Berlin, while Hoffenheim host promoted Schalke. dwi/ea

top.description: Napoli celebrate after Lazio midfielder Alfonso Pedraza scores an own goal in the Italian Serie A football match in Naples (CARLO HERMANN) Serie A leaders Lazio dropped points for just the second time this season in Sunday's 1-1 draw away to struggling Napoli, while AC Milan climbed into the top four with a 2-1 win at Genoa. Davide Frattesi gave the Romans a deserved lead but Napoli drew level early in the second half through an Alfonso Pedraza own goal. Napoli were under pressure to deliver a result after defeats by Juventus and Porto saw the squad sent into a training retreat in a bid to revive their flagging form. But they could only claim a point against Gennaro Gattuso's unbeaten outfit, whose remarkable form continued as they moved two points clear on top on 29 points, 14 ahead of Napoli in 10th place. "We must keep going, everything's not lost even if we are behind in the standings," Napoli head coach Massimiliano Allegri told DAZN. "We are not out of the race for the top four, the Coppa Italia or the Champions League. There are difficult moments over the course of a season, and they must be faced calmly." The visitors, targeting a seventh league win in a row and fifth consecutive away victory in Naples, started strongly as Gustav Isaksen and Josip Sutalo drew diving saves from Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. The Romans went in front in the 28th minute when Frattesi raced on to Tijjani Noslin's through ball and finished emphatically for his fourth goal of the season. Lazio's opener sparked a reaction from Napoli as Christos Mandas denied Rasmus Hojlund before half-time substitute Pedraza inadvertently turned a cross into his own net early in the second half. The hosts came closest to a winner as Scott McTominay tested Mandas with a low shot before Kevin De Bruyne saw a shot charged down by the Greek goalkeeper and the rebound cleared off the line by Reda Belahyane. - Milan bounce back - Milan moved above Como into fourth as Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic struck in a 2-1 victory. top.title: Kickoff time, TV network, odds announced for Arizona football’s game vs. Utah
top.description: TUCSON, AZ - NOVEMBER 06: Arizona Wildcats head coach Brent Brennan and players celebrate after a successful go ahead field goal with 38 seconds remaining in the 4th quarter of a football game between the Texas Christian University Horned Frogs and the University of Arizona Wildcats on November 06, 2026 at Casino Del Sol Stadium in Tucson, AZ. (Photo by Christopher Hook/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Arizona football will get a primetime billing for one of its biggest home games in years. Arizona and Utah will kick off at 5:30 p.m. MST at Casino Del Stadium, and the game will be televised on Fox, the Big 12 announced Sunday. Utah has opened as a 2.5-point favorite, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is 53.5 points. Arizona (7-2) needs a win over Utah in order to keep its Big 12 title game and College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Utes are coming off a rivalry victory over BYU that moved Morgan Scalley ’s team to 9-0 on the season. Arizona is hosting a top-3 team for the first time since 2007 , when No. 2 Oregon came to town — a game Arizona won in dramatic fashion. The small spread suggests oddsmakers believe Arizona can pull off a similar upset this Saturday. Arizona is just 3-6 against the spread (ATS) this season, with two of the three covers coming at home. The Wildcats failed to cover on Friday, hanging on to beat TCU 29-28 in a game they were favored to win by a touchdown. Brent Brennan ’s squad has won seven consecutive games at Casino Del Stadium, with the last loss coming in 2025 against No. 18 BYU. Arizona is 6-7 against Utah since the Utes joined the Pac-12 in 2011. All-time, the Utes have a 26-21 lead in the series. Brennan’s highest ranked win at Arizona was at Utah in 2024, when the Wildcats upset the No. 10 ranked Utes. Arizona won the previous meeting between the two schools in Tucson in 2023. Arizona and Utah didn’t play each other last year. This Utah team relies on an highly efficient offense that Arizona fans were unaccustomed to seeing in the Kyle Whittingham era. Utah ranks 13th nationally with 37.7 points per game and 12th with 215 rushing yards. Utah is 8-1 ATS. The lone game Utah didn’t cover was a 27-24 victory at Colorado. Utah quarterback Devon Dampier , a Phoenix native, has 2,053 passing yards including 20 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has another 480 yards on the ground including seven rushing scores.

nigeria.title: FG secures $200m World Bank funding to boost fish production
nigeria.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has secured a $200 million World Bank-backed financing commitment to boost fish production across the country through state governments, as part of efforts to reduce import dependence and strengthen Nigeria’s aquaculture industry. The funding, to be made available to state governments as concessional loans, is expected to support investments in fisheries and aquaculture, expand production capacity and create opportunities for private-sector participation. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, disclosed this at a high-level executive training on the Aquaculture Investment Guide organised by the ministry in collaboration with the World Bank Group in Abuja. Oyetola, who was represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Marine and Blue Economy, Prof. Busayo Fakinlede, said the financing would help states unlock their fisheries potential and develop commercially viable aquaculture projects. The minister, in a statement issued by his Special Adviser, Bolaji Akinola, said the Federal Government was prioritising collaboration with state governments, investors and development partners to position Nigeria as a fish-sufficient nation. He said expanding domestic fish production had become imperative to address the widening gap between local supply and consumption. According to him, the involvement of state governments is critical to achieving the country’s fish production targets. “Fish is a pillar of food security, household nutrition and rural livelihoods. No nation can call itself food secure while it imports most of the fish it eats. Our ambition is to produce more, import less and, in time, become a net exporter. That ambition can be achieved only when every state plays its part,” he said. Under the proposed framework, states are expected to identify priority aquaculture value chains, assess investment opportunities, develop bankable projects and commit to measurable contributions towards national fish production. Oyetola said the executive training was designed to equip state policymakers and technical officials with the expertise to translate investment opportunities into viable projects. He said the programme would focus on business models, risk management, environmental safeguards and public-private partnerships. The minister commended the World Bank Group for its support for Nigeria’s marine and blue economy development, particularly in analytical studies, capacity building and the development of the Aquaculture Investment Guide. He also disclosed plans to convene a stakeholders’ roundtable after the training to strengthen engagement with state governments, investors and development partners and establish implementation arrangements for the financing initiative. Meanwhile, Fakinlede said the ministry had increased national fish production from 1.1 million tonnes to 1.4 million tonnes through interventions aimed at strengthening the sector. nigeria.title: Navy uncovers 68,175 litres of suspected stolen crude in Rivers
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has uncovered approximately 68,175 litres of suspected stolen crude oil at illegal storage and refining sites in Ogbogolo Community, Ahoada West Local Government Area of Rivers State. The discoveries were made during two separate operations conducted on October 24 and November 7, 2026, by personnel of the Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Soroh under Operation Delta Sentinel. The Director of Information, Nigerian Navy, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the operations followed credible intelligence on illegal petroleum storage and refining activities within the Orashi Forest and adjoining areas. According to him, the naval team, during the October 24 operation, discovered two crude oil storage sites containing four dugout pits, 29 sacks and a 25-litre keg, with an estimated 8,675 litres of suspected crude oil. He said a subsequent operation on November 7 led to the discovery of two illegal refining sites comprising two large and 36 small dugout pits, alongside other storage facilities containing an estimated 59,500 litres of suspected stolen crude oil. Folorunsho said the discovered petroleum products and associated items were handled in accordance with established procedures. He explained that the operations underscored the Navy’s sustained intelligence-led efforts under Operation Delta Sentinel to dismantle illegal petroleum storage and refining infrastructure, disrupt crude oil theft networks and deny criminal elements access to the nation’s natural resources. He added that the Navy would maintain operational pressure in identified areas of criminal activity to support the protection of critical oil and gas infrastructure and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. The Navy, he said, remained committed to sustaining the operations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to combat crude oil theft, disrupt illegal refining activities and protect the nation’s maritime and economic interests. nigeria.title: Kaduna-Kano rail line ready for December 3 inauguration — APC
nigeria.description: …Kano-Katsina-Maradi project reaches 70% completion The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council has said the Kaduna-Kano Standard Gauge Railway will be inaugurated on December 3, 2026, as the Federal Government accelerates the completion of major railway projects in Northern Nigeria. The council also disclosed that the 203-kilometre Kaduna-Zaria-Kano railway project had reached approximately 90 per cent completion, while the 400-kilometre Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway project had attained 70 per cent completion. In a statement on Sunday, signed by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the projects demonstrated President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to expanding railway infrastructure, improving regional connectivity and facilitating the movement of passengers and goods. It said the Kano-Katsina-Maradi project was barely five per cent complete when Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while the Kaduna-Kano railway was less than 30 per cent complete. According to the statement, the Kaduna-Kano railway, an extension of the existing Abuja-Kaduna standard gauge line, will establish a continuous rail connection between Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano, linking major commercial centres in Northern Nigeria. The council said the two projects were recently inspected on the directive of the President by a Federal Government delegation led by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Engr. Funso Adebiyi. It said Adebiyi expressed satisfaction with the quality of construction work, particularly the railway alignment, drainage infrastructure, embankment protection, stone pitching and soil stabilisation. The inspection also included a train test run from Jaji in Kaduna State to Kano to assess the completed track infrastructure and passenger comfort. The statement added that Tinubu had directed the immediate resolution of outstanding land acquisition and compensation issues within Kaduna metropolis to facilitate the completion of the railway corridor from Abuja to Kano. It further disclosed that the completed 190-kilometre Jaji-Kano section of the Kaduna-Kano railway and the 250-kilometre Dawanu-Kano-Kazaure-Daura-Katsina section of the Kano-Maradi project would be inaugurated on December 3, 2026. When fully operational, the Kaduna-Kano railway is expected to improve passenger transportation, facilitate commercial activities and provide an alternative to road travel along one of Northern Nigeria’s busiest commercial corridors. Similarly, the Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway is expected to strengthen cross-border transportation and trade between Nigeria and neighbouring Niger Republic. The council reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to completing ongoing infrastructure projects across the country in line with its development agenda. nigeria.title: Ibom Deep Sea Port: NDC questions Tinubu’s fresh approval
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has questioned the latest approval of the proposed Ibom Deep Sea Port by President Bola Tinubu, recalling that the project had earlier received approval under former President Muhammadu Buhari in December 2020. The opposition party accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of making repeated promises on the project without delivering on previous commitments, asking how many times the Federal Government would approve the same port. In a statement on Sunday, signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the NDC recalled that the Federal Executive Council (FEC), under Buhari, had on December 16, 2020, approved the implementation of the first phase of the $4.6 billion Ibom Deep Sea Port project. It said the approval named Bollore/Power China as the preferred bidder and was intended to pave the way for the commencement of construction. The statement, titled, “APC’s Endless Lies and Deceit: How Many Times Will APC Approve Ibom Deep Sea Port?”, followed Tinubu’s announcement of approval for the proposed port during his visit to Akwa Ibom State on November 6, 2026. The NDC also recalled that Tinubu, as the APC presidential candidate, had promised to build the port during the party’s campaign rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on January 30, 2023. Quoting the President’s campaign remarks, the party said he had told supporters: “We will do mechanised farming. We will export food from Akwa Ibom. We will build your seaport.” It, however, accused the APC of failing to fulfil the promise, arguing that the latest announcement amounted to a fresh commitment on a project that had already received federal approval. “In a brazen display of ignorance of statecraft and the elevation of grand deceit as a campaign strategy, President Tinubu, as APC presidential candidate, first promised the port during his 2023 campaign,” the party said. The NDC described the latest announcement as another promise that might not be fulfilled, urging Nigerians to hold the ruling party accountable for its previous commitments. Drawing a comparison with the Federal Government’s electricity supply promises, the opposition party said residents of Akwa Ibom were still waiting for the proposed deep sea port despite the earlier approval. It also urged Nigerians to reject the APC in future elections, declaring that a new Nigeria was possible under the NDC. nigeria.description: …Taskforce impounds 128 motorcycles in fresh clampdown By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Taskforce has arrested a 36-year-old former operative, Adeyemo Olalekan, for allegedly impersonating a serving official of the agency to seize commercial motorcycles and extort their operators. The suspect, who was reportedly dismissed from the agency several years ago over theft-related misconduct, was arrested on Sunday following a tip-off received through the Taskforce’s official hotlines. The agency said preliminary investigations revealed that Olalekan had allegedly continued to pose as a Taskforce operative despite his dismissal, conducting illegal arrests and demanding money from victims in exchange for the release of their motorcycles. A victim, who became suspicious of his activities, reportedly contacted the agency and subsequently discovered that the suspect was no longer in its employment. Speaking on the arrest, the Chairman of the Lagos State Taskforce, Chief Superintendent of Police (CSP) Adetayo Akerele, said operatives apprehended the suspect while he was allegedly attempting to extort two commercial motorcycle operators whose motorcycles he had unlawfully impounded. Akerele said the suspect had evaded arrest on several previous occasions before his eventual apprehension. He added that the agency had been tracking individuals involved in similar fraudulent activities following repeated complaints from members of the public. The chairman described the impostors as criminal elements who exploit the identity and authority of the Taskforce to unlawfully apprehend motorcycle operators and demand money for the release of their motorcycles. According to the agency, the suspect allegedly targeted brand-new Bajaj motorcycles and motorcycles with engine capacities below 200cc, particularly those operating on highways and other restricted routes. He reportedly confessed to disguising himself as a genuine passenger, approaching unsuspecting motorcycle riders and paying their fares before suddenly identifying himself as an enforcement officer. The suspect would then allegedly threaten to have their motorcycles crushed unless they paid him money. He has since been arraigned before a court on three counts bordering on impersonation, extortion and conduct likely to cause a breach of public peace. The agency said he pleaded guilty to all three charges, while the case was adjourned until December 16, 2026, for facts and sentencing. He was subsequently remanded at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre. Akerele reiterated the agency’s determination to rid Lagos of individuals exploiting its identity to engage in criminal activities, warning that dismissed personnel and other impostors would be made to face the law. nigeria.title: Lagos seals Surulere church over noise pollution
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has sealed The All Christians Gathering Ministry in Surulere over alleged noise pollution and violations of environmental regulations. The church, located at No. 1, Ishola Street, off Clegg, Surulere, was shut on Sunday following an investigation which reportedly established that its activities violated environmental regulations and constituted a nuisance to residents. The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, announced the closure in a statement on his X account, saying the action followed a complaint by a resident identified as DAVERY (@BigDavery) over persistent noise from the church. “Following a complaint by @BigDavery regarding noise pollution from a church, our officials conducted an investigation and confirmed that the church was in violation of environmental regulations and constituted a nuisance to residents in the area,” Wahab said. He added that the facility had been sealed and would remain closed until further notice. The commissioner said the state government would not tolerate environmental violations or activities that disrupted the peace and well-being of residents, stressing that religious institutions, businesses and other establishments must comply with environmental regulations. The enforcement action followed a series of complaints by the resident, who had taken to X in the early hours of Saturday to report noise which he said had repeatedly disrupted his sleep. In one of his posts, made at about 1:31 a.m., the complainant appealed to Wahab to intervene, sharing videos of the noise and offering to provide the church’s address privately for security reasons. In earlier posts, the resident also alleged that a member of the church had threatened him after he confronted the ministry over the noise. He further expressed concern about the impact on other residents, including a household with a child under one year old. The complainant also said the noise had forced him to keep his windows shut at night despite the heat and lack of electricity to operate a fan. The closure forms part of the Lagos State Government’s efforts to enforce environmental regulations and curb noise pollution across the state. Under Lagos State environmental regulations, permissible noise levels in residential areas are 55 decibels during the day and 45 decibels at night. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. sports.description: NEW DELHI: India’s Under-19 batter Arjun Rajput came to his team's rescue with a brilliant century against Pakistan in the U-19 Asia Cup on Sunday. Anvay Dravid, son of former India captain and coach Rahul Dravid, also failed to make a significant contribution. With wickets falling at the other end, Rajput took responsibility and played attacking cricket. He used sweeps against spinners and played aerial shots against fast bowlers to put pressure back on Pakistan. He scored 107 off 85 balls, hitting 11 fours and five sixes, before getting dismissed. His innings helped India reach 208 before being bowled out in 46.3 overs. Who is Arjun Rajput? He had an impressive run in the 2026-27 Under-19 Vinoo Mankad Trophy, where he scored 695 runs in eight innings and helped Punjab win the title. Speaking about his son's journey, he told NDTV Sports, “I have been making kulchas for many years. Arjun has been playing cricket since the age of five years. sports.title: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Ben Shelton in thrilling final for first Paris Masters title
sports.description: Carlos Alcaraz ’s excellent comeback continued as he defeated Ben Shelton 7-6(5) 7-5 to claim the Paris Masters title for the first time. World No 3 Alcaraz missed nearly five months of the 2026 season with a wrist injury and his initial comeback came to an end at Shelton’s hands, with the American triumphing in a epic five-setter in the US Open quarter-finals. Since then Alcaraz has lifted ATP 500 titles in Tokyo and Vienna, the latter just last week. Despite not playing at his fluid best he scraped through in Paris - saving two match points against Taylor Fritz in the quarter-finals - and he continued his late-season surge with victory in an entertaining encounter between two of the tour’s flair players and his first meeting with Shelton since New York. Shelton made an assured start on serve and it was Alcaraz who came under pressure first, falling 0-40 down as the American led 2-1. But the Spaniard saved four break points to hold in a near eight-minute game, with a combination of deft volleys and aggression from the back of the court. Both players struggled to take their chances as Shelton saved two break points - one with a sublime angled volley - to keep things on serve for a 4-3 lead, then spurned another two chances to break before Alcaraz held for 4-4 with a punishing, unreturned first serve. Inevitably the first set went to a tiebreak, a contest of frequent momentum swings as eight of the 12 points went against serve. Shelton battled back from 1-3 down with an explosive smash while back-pedalling to the baseline, but could not press his advantage home. Alcaraz set up two set points with a fierce backhand volley, spurning the first thanks to an unhelpful net cord which just dipped back onto his side, but let out a roar of relief as Shelton blasted a forehand wide to concede the first set 7-6(5) in just over an hour. US Open runner-up Shelton won his previous three matches in Paris in three sets and would be forced to attempt another escape act, starting from 0-30 down in his first service game of the second set. Ben Shelton's athleticism and serve posed problems (Getty) Four big first serves helped him out of trouble and he was rewarded for his patience as he finally broke Alcaraz’s serve for a 3-2 lead, the first break of the match, with a fierce angled return that Alcaraz could only send long. A superb overhead smash from the American in the next game led to the first sign of genuine frustration for Alcaraz, who mimed throwing his racquet to the ground, as Shelton held to love. sports.title: Garcia, Schick take Leverkusen to derby win at Cologne
sports.description: Freiburg can climb to third spot with a win at home over strugglers Union Berlin on Sunday (Silas Stein) Goals from Aleix Garcia and Patrik Schick took Bayer Leverkusen to a tense 2-1 derby win at Cologne on Sunday, lifting the visitors to fifth in the Bundesliga table. Garcia curled an excellent effort into the top corner after just seven minutes and Schick scored five minutes from time in a fiery encounter which produced 11 yellow cards, including six for the hosts. Germany starlet Said El Mala scored a stoppage-time consolation goal for the hosts, who sit in 15th spot, just one clear of the relegation playoff placing. One of several derbies in Germany's football-mad north-west, Cologne and Leverkusen are just 10 kilometres (six miles) apart. The travelling support teased the hosts with chants referring to the 2023-24 season, when Leverkusen won their maiden Bundesliga title and Cologne were relegated. Leverkusen broke through just seven minutes in when Garcia's free-kick flew over the wall and into the top-left corner, with a helpless Cologne goalie Marvin Schwaebe watching on. Just before the break, the Spaniard found Jarell Quansah in space but the England centre-back headed just wide. Well handled by the Leverkusen defence, the hosts grew increasingly frustrated, picking up five of their six yellow cards in the second-half. Schick had a goal rubbed out for handball with ten minutes to go but broke through just five minutes later, slotting in on the counter for an eighth goal in nine league games this season. El Mala scored one of his own in stoppage time but the goal came too late to launch a Cologne comeback. Later on Sunday, Freiburg can climb to third spot with a win at home over strugglers Union Berlin, while Hoffenheim host promoted Schalke. dwi/ea

technology.title: Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
technology.description: Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don't agree on why. In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate. The missing electrons Central to the mystery of cuprates’ high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. “The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons,” Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be. “Everybody knows that from different probes, you see that there's these vanishing electrons, but nobody knows why,” Allan said. technology.title: Doom delivers five minutes of terminal violence on an IBM mainframe
technology.description: Can an IBM Z mainframe run Doom? Of course it can. The more interesting question is whether you can play it through a text terminal without ruining your eyesight. WND Software's browser demo connects to an IBM Z mainframe over SSH using its terminal emulator. Wojciech Graj's DOOM-ASCII supplies the text-based carnage, replacing conventional graphics with colored characters. There's no sound. It is, however, completely playable (although you might need to recalibrate your vision to work out what is going on, particularly with regard to distant objects). Sessions are limited to five minutes, with room for up to 50 simultaneous users, but we had no trouble getting in. ASCII also presented no issues once the game was in motion. This writer played the original shareware release on an Amstrad ALT386SX portable, so squinting at an indistinct demon felt reassuringly familiar. That Doom can be persuaded to run on an IBM Z mainframe is not particularly noteworthy. The code has turned up everywhere from databases to PCB designers . Even the humble Pi Pico was roped into the fun. Keeping the action playable through a text terminal is the more entertaining achievement. A year ago, an IBM consultant persuaded Doom to run on IBM Z and LinuxONE using VNC to bring the pixelated mayhem to life. Using a terminal emulator, while a neat demonstration of the capabilities of WND's software, is perhaps more an example of "because I can" masochism. It's undeniably an enjoyable way to burn through five minutes. No installation or login required – just a willingness to shoot at punctuation. ®

technology.title: Internet governance about to get its quadrennial stress test at ITU meeting
technology.description: The International Telecommunications Union (ITU) kicks off its quadrennial plenipotentiary on Monday, and internet governance organizations are bracing in case the event becomes a forum for nation-states to try to challenge their roles. The ITU is the United Nations' specialized agency for information and communication technologies, meaning its members are nation-states. The body's role is to facilitate international connectivity, which it does by managing radio spectrum, satellite orbits, and working on relevant technical standards. Its key standards are pervasive. ITU-T X.509 sets out the rules of public key infrastructure. ITU-T E.164 governs telephone numbers. ITU-T H.264 and 265 define the video codecs used for most online streams. The ITU's role is largely uncontested, yet its work gets very close to that of the organizations who work on technologies that make the internet work. Those bodies include the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF); the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), which oversees the domain name system; and the regional internet registries (RIRs), which manage IP addresses. The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) works on HTML, CSS, and accessibility. Governments participate in work at those internet governance bodies but are just one voice among many and can't override the consensus-driven decision-making process they use, under a system which has come to be known as the multi-stakeholder governance model. At a 2025 event called WSIS+20, the United Nations endorsed multi-stakeholder governance by deciding that its Internet Governance Forum (IGF) should become a permanent body. That decision effectively endorsed multi-stakeholder governance, and kept the ITU out of internet standards. Yet the IGF hasn't met since WSIS+20, so it is yet to start operating meaningfully as a permanent body. This year's ITU meeting is therefore a moment at which stakeholders can stress-test the delicate balance between the ITU, internet governance bodies, and the emerging IGF. Such a test could see ITU members try to have it pursue new fields that overlap with work performed by internet governance organizations. This has already happened before. China tried to have the ITU work on " New IP" – a major revision to internet protocol, a technology the IETF manages. In 2022, Russia and China backed a candidate for the ITU presidency who favored giving nations a stronger role in internet governance, potentialy by having the ITU take over some standards work. That candidate was not elected. Ahead of next week's meetings, the Internet Society published a background paper that declared it is "actively challenging proposals that could affect the Internet's underlying technical architecture or increase fragmentation, as well as those that could affect connectivity, particularly for remote, underserved, and unserved communities." science.description: null "Starlog" was one of the greatest sci-fi and fantasy magazines ever, and after a 17-year absence, it's being resurrected. The legendary sci-fi mag went dark back in 2009 as part of the wave of popular publications folding due to years of declining readership and subscriptions. But as of Nov. 13, this geek favorite periodical returns as an annual print edition, and it's available for pre-order now. It’s another indication of digital fatigue in the world, and fans of a certain age will recall the pleasure of poring over each colorful issue packed with in-depth interviews, behind-the-scenes photos, TV guides, classic movie retrospectives, book reviews, con news, and VFX features. The triumphant relaunch of "Starlog" magazine happens on Nov. 13, 2026 (Image credit: Fangoria Holdings) "Starlog" launched in 1976, in the pre-" Star Wars " days, under the leadership of editor-in-chief Terry O’Quinn. It first arrived with artist Jack Thurston's beautiful painted "Star Trek" cover, featuring William Shatner as Captain James T. Kirk and Leonard Nimoy’s Spock, set against the U.S.S. Enterprise near a shimmering black hole. The magazine continued to inform the science fiction community about upcoming sci-fi TV shows and blockbuster Hollywood films for over three decades; I fondly recall reading each informative and entertaining monthly issue cover-to-cover. Just in time to honor its 50th anniversary this year, "Starlog" blasts back into the sci-fi universe with Issue #375 showcasing cover artwork created by Armenian artist Gabriel Yeganyan. Its geek culture legacy, covering iconic franchises like "Star Wars," "Star Trek," and "Alien," will now live on thanks to Fangoria Holdings and io9 co-founder Annalee Newitz, editor-in-chief. Three vintage "Starlog" magazine issues from my personal collection! (Image credit: Jeff Spry) "During its original 33-year run, 'Starlog' documented science fiction as it evolved across film, television, books, technology, and culture," said 'Fangoria's Tara Ansley. "Fifty years after the magazine first launched, the line between science fiction and the real world has become increasingly difficult to separate. That makes this an especially interesting time to bring 'Starlog' back. Technology may change, but the most compelling questions have always been about people: how we live, what we create, and what kind of future we want to build." "Starlog" reloads for its first annual edition after a long hiatus on Nov. 13. You can pre-order the first issue (Issue 375 in continuity) on the Starlog website .

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
science.description: null On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this. It performed well, but eventually it stopped listening to commands. The spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere in January 2015. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the Venus Express spacecraft to Venus on Nov. 8, 2005.. (Image credit: ESA) Why it mattered Venus Express established ESA as the third world organization to successfully send a probe to study Venus, following the United States and Soviet Union. (Japan's JAXA became the fourth five years later.) "By studying Venus, scientists learn how Earth-like planets change over time," reads a summary of the planet's exploration prepared by The Planetary Society. "Orbital studies [like Venus Express] hint that Venus may have hosted habitable oceans before becoming inhospitable." "By studying Venus, we can learn how Earth-like planets evolve and what shapes planets throughout the galaxy into temperate, lush worlds instead of sweltering hothouses. Venus also helps scientists model Earth’s climate, and may serve as a cautionary tale on how dramatically a planet’s climate can change," wrote the Society. An illustration of the Venus Express spacecraft in orbit around Venus. (Image credit: ESA) ESA returned to Venus in 2018 when BepiColombo, its joint mission with JAXA, used the planet's gravity to redirect its path toward the planet Mercury. Want more space history? science.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
science.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. An illustration shows the landscape of a primordial Earth before life arose as lightning splits the skies (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) What makes the simulation especially useful is its plug-and-play nature. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . science.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed. "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. science.title: SpaceX launches mystery mission for US Space Force in gorgeous sunset liftoff from California (video, photos)
science.description: null SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. The Falcon 9's first stage after its landing on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1095 missions GPS-III 8 | 6 Starlink missions USSF-432 was the 119th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, and the 14th national-security flight of the rocket so far this year. The vast majority of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 — more than 70% — have been devoted to building out the Starlink megaconstellation. SpaceX has also launched six other missions this year. Three were operational flights of the company's Falcon Heavy rocket, while the other three were test missions of its next-gen Starship vehicle. SpaceX plans to retire both the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy shortly after the fully reusable Starship, the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, is up and running.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so.
